title: Clean developer setup
input: Fresh supported Python environment
expected: Installation, import and documented test commands succeed.

title: Synthetic corpus provenance
input: Normal, invalid and localisation scenarios
expected: No copied game content.
Inputs and expected outputs are deterministic and labelled synthetic.

title: Invalid configuration
input: Missing, inaccessible and malformed settings
expected: Structured diagnostics and no unrelated filesystem scan.

title: Runtime and path diagnostics
input: Overlapping game/output paths and missing FTS
expected: Unsafe paths rejected.
Capabilities and fallback reported.

title: Deterministic inventory
input: Same bytes at different absolute roots
expected: Same content fingerprint and relative paths.
Original bytes unchanged.

title: Filesystem containment
input: Traversal, symlink escape, excess size/depth/count
expected: Rejected without writes outside owned data directory.

title: Version uncertainty
input: Missing metadata and user-reported version
expected: Unknown and user_reported remain distinguishable; build ID is not a patch label.

title: DLC state separation
input: DLC files present without ownership or activation evidence
expected: Installed, owned and enabled are separate tri-state fields.

title: String and comment tokens
input: Braces and comment markers inside escaped strings
expected: Correct tokens and exact original spans.

title: Encoding and line offsets
input: UTF-8 BOM, CRLF and invalid bytes
expected: Original byte/line positions preserved.
Invalid decoding is explicit.

title: Ordered duplicate AST
input: Duplicate assignments and scalar/assignment mixed blocks
expected: Order and all occurrences preserved.

title: Unknown script syntax
input: Unsupported operators and expression forms
expected: Raw input retained and diagnostic emitted without invented semantics.

title: Malformed and deep script
input: Unclosed strings/braces and excessive nesting
expected: Bounded error recovery; no false successful parse.

title: Technology extraction
input: Synthetic technology with conditions and prerequisites
expected: ID, raw expressions, condition structure and source refs match expected data.

title: Language fallback
input: Korean, English-only and missing translation
expected: Requested language then English then ID, with explicit provenance.

title: Localisation cycle
input: Self reference and two-key cycle
expected: Resolution stops with cycle diagnostic.

title: Localisation duplicates and dynamic text
input: Repeated keys, formatting tags and dynamic expressions
expected: Raw values retained; ambiguity and unsupported rendering shown.

title: Snapshot identity and schema
input: Identical corpus and changed parser/policy/schema
expected: Identity stable for same inputs and distinct when relevant policy changes.

title: Atomic snapshot activation
input: Writer failure, cancellation and concurrent writer
expected: Building data not queried; previous active remains usable.

title: Exact retrieval
input: ID, Korean/English names and explicit aliases
expected: Correct entity first with stable ties and match reason.

title: Short Korean and normalization
input: Two-character Korean, NFC variants and missing FTS
expected: Explicit fallback retrieves expected entity without claiming morphology support.

title: Query metacharacters
input: Quotes, parentheses, operators, empty and oversized query
expected: No SQL or FTS syntax injection; invalid input receives bounded diagnostics.

title: Citation correctness
input: Synthetic fields with different definition and translation sources
expected: Every fact points to the exact supporting bytes and lines.

title: Not found and unsupported answers
input: Absent ID, dynamic costs and research probability request
expected: No invented fact, number or probability.

title: Snapshot and branch isolation
input: Same ID in different snapshots and beta/stable context
expected: Results do not leak across selected context; unknown version remains unknown.

title: CLI contract
input: Init, doctor, index, search, show and snapshots on synthetic data
expected: Valid JSON stdout, separate logs, documented exit codes and read-only input.

title: Domain adapter coverage
input: Each scoped non-technology domain with conflict and error examples
expected: IDs, fields, names, conditions and sources are correct; support gaps explicit.

title: Unresolved references
input: Missing and ambiguous prerequisite/event targets
expected: Typed unresolved/ambiguous edges without invented targets.

title: Reference cycles
input: Cyclic references and depth limit
expected: Traversal terminates and reports limits; graph is not an execution simulation.

title: Incremental changes
input: Added, changed and removed files and entities
expected: New snapshot matches a full rebuild and old snapshot remains consistent.

title: Sources change during indexing
input: Change a source between capture and activation
expected: Activation aborted or retried safely; mixed-time data is not declared ready.

title: Offline and original-file safety
input: Network blocked and originals read-only during all v0.1 flows
expected: No outbound calls or source writes; basic search still works.

title: Private data and instruction text
input: Synthetic secret/path markers and instruction-like input text
expected: Public logs redact markers; input text has no execution authority.

title: Evaluation runner integrity
input: At least 40 balanced questions and automated v0.1 cases E-001 through E-036
expected: Repeatable results, recall@5 and exact/abstention metrics with evidence.
No test marked pass without execution.

title: Performance measurements
input: 10000 synthetic entities and repeated cold/warm queries
expected: Environment, corpus hash, raw samples and p95 recorded; no unmeasured performance claims.

title: Packaged platform smoke
input: Clean Linux and Windows environments
expected: Installable package, CLI workflow and exact test matrix recorded.

title: Actual installation acceptance
input: User-local game data with version evidence
expected: Read-only supported-domain checks, coverage and limitations documented without publishing originals.

title: Release checklist
input: Required evidence and documented release candidate
expected: All mandatory gates checked; preview and validated release distinguished; approval recorded.

title: Official news freshness
input: Dated official/beta posts, timeout, rate limit and offline cache
expected: Dates/channels/platforms separated; failed check is not no-change or fresh.

title: Provider consent and fallback
input: Provider absent, declined consent, timeout and budget limit
expected: Deterministic fallback and no unauthorized transmission or charge.

title: LLM evidence enforcement
input: Invented citation/number and instructions inside retrieved content
expected: Unsupported output rejected or replaced by static evidence; no tool escalation.

title: Mod context evidence
input: Installed but inactive mods and unknown order
expected: Installed, enabled and order states remain separate and evidenced.

title: Mod replacement semantics
input: Category-specific replacement and multiple conflicting definitions
expected: Effective result only for validated rules; unresolved cases retained.

title: Save and archive limits
input: Supported and unknown format, excessive compression and unsafe paths
expected: Bounded read-only parsing; unknown field meanings not used as facts.

title: Calculation reference cases
input: Documented inputs, units, formulas and boundary cases
expected: Results match reference cases within stated tolerance; missing inputs stop claims.

title: Local UI boundary
input: Local access, untrusted text and invalid paths
expected: Loopback default, escaped rendering, restricted paths and same service results.

title: Review safety regressions and main-line integration
input: Unowned/linked generator output, invalid path inputs, inaccessible directory traversal, public diagnostic secrets, XDG edge values and main-line integration
expected: No unowned files are deleted and output or internal symlink escapes are rejected.
Tampered manifests cannot expand ownership outside corpus/.
Unmanaged files that collide with generated paths are never overwritten.
Unmanaged empty directories are preserved.
User path failures return structured diagnostics without traceback.
Directory traversal permissions are checked where required.
Public serialization contains no protected path values.
Empty or relative XDG values fall back safely and schema_version is strictly integer.
The final main-targeting integration SHA passes Linux and Windows CI.
